about.title: About SEMA
about.text: The Somalia Explosive Management Authority is the national institution responsible for leading and coordinating mine action and explosive hazard management across Somalia.
about.lead0: SEMA works with government institutions, Federal Member States, operators, communities, and international partners to strengthen public safety, improve coordination, support information management, and reduce the impact of explosive hazards on people, services, livelihoods, and development.
about.lead1: SEMA provides official public information through its national website, including mine action news, policy publications, data dashboards, data access services, and direct contact channels for government institutions, partners, and the public.

mandate.title: National authority for mine action coordination and explosive hazard management.
mandate.text: SEMA's mandate covers the full spectrum of mine action functions — from national coordination and operator oversight to information management, risk education, victim assistance, and treaty reporting.
mandate.area0Text: SEMA leads and coordinates all national mine action activities, aligning government institutions, Federal Member States, operators, donors, and technical partners around shared priorities.
mandate.area1Text: SEMA oversees the systematic identification, marking, and clearance of explosive hazards including anti-personnel mines, cluster munitions, and explosive remnants of war.
mandate.area2Text: SEMA develops and maintains national information management systems to collect, validate, analyse, and share mine action data for planning, operations, and public reporting.
mandate.area3Text: SEMA establishes and monitors national standards, accreditation requirements, and quality management processes for all operators conducting mine action activities in Somalia.
mandate.area4Text: SEMA coordinates explosive ordnance risk education programmes that reduce casualties by informing communities about the dangers of explosive hazards and safe behaviours.
mandate.area5Text: SEMA supports victim assistance efforts by coordinating services, strengthening national reporting, and advocating for the rights and needs of landmine and EO survivors.
mandate.area6Text: SEMA fulfils Somalia's international treaty reporting obligations, including annual Article 7 reports under the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention and related instruments.
mandate.area7Text: SEMA leads the development and implementation of national mine action strategies, work plans, and sectoral priorities aligned with Somalia's development and security agenda.
mandate.area8Text: SEMA facilitates coordination with Federal Member States, UN agencies, international NGOs, and bilateral donors supporting mine action and explosive hazard management in Somalia.
mandate.gov0: Maintain a national overview of mine action priorities and public reporting needs.
mandate.gov1: Support standards, accreditation, and quality management for operators.
mandate.gov2: Coordinate with Federal Member States and partners on planning and implementation.
mandate.gov3: Publish verified information through reports, dashboards, and official updates.

leadership.title: Senior Management of SEMA
leadership.text: SEMA is led by senior government officials appointed by the Federal Government of Somalia to direct national mine action coordination, policy, and institutional oversight.
leadership.bio0: The Director General provides strategic direction and national leadership for Somalia's mine action coordination, reporting to the Federal Government and overseeing all SEMA operations and programmes.
leadership.bio1: The Deputy Director General supports the Director General in institutional oversight, inter-agency coordination, and representation at national and international forums.
leadership.bio2: The Director of Operations oversees field coordination, operator management, clearance task prioritisation, and quality assurance across all mine action operations in Somalia.
leadership.bio3: The Director of Information Management leads SEMA's national data systems, IMSMA coordination, reporting infrastructure, and open data initiatives.
leadership.bio4: The Director of Standards & Quality establishes accreditation requirements, monitors compliance, and maintains national mine action standards aligned with IMAS and treaty obligations.
leadership.bio5: The Director of EORE & Victim Assistance coordinates explosive ordnance risk education programmes and national victim assistance services across Federal Member States.

dataRequest.title: Request SEMA data through a transparent review process.
dataRequest.text: Government institutions, operators, researchers, donors, media, humanitarian partners, and the public can request mine action information through this official form.
dataRequest.formText: Submit enough detail for SEMA to understand the data need, intended use, requested format, and any deadline.
dataRequest.step0Text: Complete the form with the requested dataset, geography, time period, purpose, and preferred format.
dataRequest.step1Text: SEMA receives the request and can issue a reference number for follow-up.
dataRequest.step2Text: The request is reviewed for sensitivity, data availability, mandate, intended use, and release conditions.
dataRequest.step3Text: SEMA may contact the requester for more details or recommend a public alternative.
dataRequest.step4Text: Approved requests can be fulfilled by email, secure download link, dashboard access, or data-sharing agreement.
dataRequest.restricted0: Exact hazard coordinates or data that could create security or public safety risks.
dataRequest.restricted1: Personally identifiable information or victim/survivor records.
dataRequest.restricted2: Unpublished operational records or partner-restricted datasets.
dataRequest.restricted3: Information requiring formal authorization or a data-sharing agreement.
dataRequest.name: Full name
dataRequest.dataRequestedPlaceholder: Describe the data, indicators, geography, period, and level of detail requested.
dataRequest.intendedUsePlaceholder: Explain how the data will be used and who will access it.
dataRequest.terms: I understand that sensitive, personal, security-related, or restricted operational data may be declined, aggregated, or shared only through an approved agreement.
dataRequest.successNoRef: Your request was submitted for review.

privacy.title: Analytics and dashboard-access privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what information SEMA collects when you browse this website and when you access a SEMA Power BI or ArcGIS dashboard, why it is collected, and how it is handled.

whatWebsite.title: Website analytics
whatWebsite.body: When you browse this website, SEMA records anonymous, aggregate information: pages visited, navigation links and buttons clicked, publications downloaded, external links clicked, the language you use, the site that referred you, and the approximate date and time of your visit. We also generate a random, first-party identifier stored in your browser so that repeat visits from the same browser can be counted — this identifier is not linked to your name, email address, or any other personal information.

whatDashboard.title: Dashboard-access information
whatDashboard.body: Before opening a SEMA mine action dashboard, we ask for your organization name, areas of activity, and — optionally — your organization type and country of operation. This information helps SEMA understand who is using its dashboards, improve its information products, and support stakeholder engagement. It is never displayed publicly.

location.title: Approximate location
location.body: Where available from our hosting infrastructure, we record an approximate country, region, and city associated with your visit. We do not request your device's GPS location, and we do not collect or store exact coordinates. We do not permanently store your raw IP address, and it is never shown in the SEMA admin area.

estimates.title: Unique visitor counts are estimates
estimates.body: Figures such as "unique visitors" reported to SEMA staff are estimates based on anonymous browser identifiers. They represent distinct browsers or devices, not verified individual people, and the same person using two devices may be counted twice.

retention.title: How long information is kept
retention.body: Dashboard-access organization records and website analytics events are retained for a limited period, configured by SEMA, after which older records are eligible for deletion. Contact SEMA using the details below for the current retention periods.

access.title: Who can see this information
access.body: Only authorized SEMA administrators can view organization-level dashboard-access records and detailed website analytics. This information is never made public and is not shared with third parties for marketing purposes.

contact.title: Questions about your data
contact.body: To ask a question about the information described in this notice, contact SEMA at info@sema.gov.so or through the contact form on this website.

powerbi.title: About Power BI dashboards
powerbi.body: This access form helps SEMA understand and engage with its stakeholders — it is not a security control. If a dashboard is published using Power BI "Publish to web", the underlying report may still be reachable directly by anyone who already has that direct link, independent of this website.
